This place is definitely worth the hype. It was so hard to get a reservation. We ended up with a 10:30pm table so it basically became our second dinner. I just wish I had been hungrier.

The truffle bread was incredible. It had a slight sweetness that paired perfectly with the butter. The steak tartare was another favorite. The bread was super crispy and complemented the tartare so well. The spicy shrimp pasta was also delicious with just the right amount of kick. The burger and fries were good but nothing standing out.

I’m usually not a huge mac and cheese person but this one completely changed my mind. It had such a rich, strong truffle flavor that made it so addictive.

For dessert the chocolate tart was great as expected but the strawberry vacherin was really good. I’m usually a chocolate dessert person but this was honestly one of my favorites. It had a crisp meringue shell with whipped cream, strawberry icecream inside, and marinated strawberries outside. so light, refreshing, and the perfect way to end the meal. We weren’t huge fans of the drinks but everything else was excellent!

I was really excited to try this restaurant out as i have heard many great things. We did not have a reservation as we know it’s extremely hard to get. So we decided to walk in around 8:45 pm and put our name down. The hostess was friendly and reassured us she can’t guarantee we get a table. We waited around and by 10 pm she came up to us and let us know that she could seat us. Shout out to her! I don’t remember her name but It’s a breath of fresh air when you get to experience nice front of house staff in this city.

Our waitress , well two of them were very nice and let us know their opinions on the menu.

We decided to order the ..
famous monkey bread 8/10 the butter is what saves the bread. But i feel like it could’ve had more flavor
Crab Rangoon 7.5/10 i thought there would be more crab filling , but the flavor was good.
Double cheeseburger 8/10 it was good but nothing to seriously rave about. I like the au cheval burger better.
Maple thick slice bacon - 9/10 it was very good! I really enjoyed the flavor profiles and the perform added a nice touch.
Fries - 7/10 nothing special just fries . The aioli was decent but kind of a tangy aftertaste.
Drinks :
Vera - really delicious, fresh yet strong !
Old fashion - hubby said he enjoyed his drink as well

We did have leftovers and i am quite disappointed to find out the man who packed out food did not include any of the condiments / sauces that went with our food. I asked him to include everything and I didn’t check the box considering I can trust someone to do their job correctly at this type of establishment , however he fell short on that part :/
Overall the experience was pleasant and I will return to try some of the other dishes!!

text.text: I am glad I checked this place off my bucket list, but there will be a lot of buts in my review. The atmosphere screams old New York and the bar area is way more fun than the dining room in my opinion. The service was top notch, but it took a very long time for our entrees to come out. I understand it was Father’s Day, but it was too long. The Monkey Bread was great, but definitely not worth the price (I am glad I tried it though). Next the French Dip, it was good, but I can think of at least 2 restaurants that have a better french dip. The double cheeseburger was great (perhaps the star), but for the price at least throw in some chips. The Mac n Cheese was very cheesy, I loved the pasta they used and top was crispy. Now our server, she was great and apologized for the slow service and even bought use complimentary ice cream. She deserves 5 stars. This place is worth trying, just expect to drop a lot of dough.

text.text:
One of the finest dining experiences of my life. We did the tasting menu at The Modern, and while it was around $350/person, it genuinely felt worth every penny.

Every course was unlike anything I’d tasted before. Unexpected combinations, incredibly complex sauces, beautiful textures, and flavors that somehow worked together perfectly. The “Egg on Egg on Egg” was especially memorable. I also loved hearing the stories behind the dishes and learning from the chef how some of the components and sauces took days to prepare. It made you appreciate just how much thought and craftsmanship went into every bite.

The portions look tiny individually, but after eight or so courses, we actually left quite full! The service was exceptional too, warm, attentive, and never stuffy. They took lovely photos of us, and we were given our menu at the end as a keepsake, which was such a nice touch.

This wasn’t just a great meal. It felt like experiencing food in an entirely new way. My tongue genuinely discovered flavors it did not know existed. An unforgettable two-Michelin-star experience at MoMA, and absolutely worth doing at least once. ❤️

I came here to celebrate my graduation, it was my first foray into fine dining and I had a great experience here. I had Alex as my server and he was amazing! He was very genuine and did a really good job at translating the menu and feel approachable without ever being overwhelming. text.text:
Hands down the best restaurant experience my wife and I have ever had.

We wanted to treat ourselves for our anniversary, and I had recently watched their Bon Appétit behind-the-scenes video. Their entire operation seemed so incredibly focused, meticulous, and inspiring that we knew we had to try it.

We started with the Iberico ham and the hiramasa tart, both incredible. Then came the chilled lobster, which was super fresh and refreshing, served with an amazing sauce that made me want to lick the plate clean. Every dish felt refined without being overly complicated.

The service was extraordinary. You can immediately tell the front-of-house team is operating at an extremely high level and is aware of everything happening in the room at all times. At one point, my wife stepped away to use the restroom just as they were about to serve the first course. Without saying a word or making anything awkward, the staff simply looped around a couple of times until she returned. The moment she sat down, they resumed service seamlessly without missing a beat. That level of awareness and professionalism really stood out to us.

Next came the rye bread, which was fresh and crispy on the outside, soft and fluffy on the inside, paired with delicious butter. Then we had the sea bass with crab, which was phenomenal and one of my favorite dishes of the night.

But the true star of the show for me was the lamb. My wife and I grill lamb racks often, and I genuinely had no idea this level of perfection existed. It was cooked flawlessly, and the sauce was absolutely incredible. If I was not in public, I probably would have been scraping the bone clean :)

Big shoutout to one of the staff members, Stephanie, who completely made our night. We were telling her how excited we were to finally visit after watching the Bon Appétit video, and she casually asked if we wanted a tour of the kitchen after dinner. Honestly, I thought she was joking at first. Then she came back after dessert and reminded us.

Even after paying the bill, I still thought maybe she was kidding, but then she walked over smiling and said, “Let’s go.”

My wife and I were completely geeked out. Seeing the kitchen in person was surreal. It was exactly like the video: super meticulous, orders being called out and repeated in unison, everyone moving with total precision and purpose. You could see the Omega clock, the Michelin stars on the wall, and just the overall culture of excellence behind everything they do. We were honestly in awe.

Thank you again, Stephanie. That experience meant so much to us.

Every time we visit a fine dining restaurant for a special occasion, I always wonder whether it will truly live up to the hype. Some completely miss the mark. Some are very good. But none have delivered on every aspect the way The Modern did.

This is officially our favorite restaurant in the world.

There’s two ways to enter this restaurant. They do in fact have a main door facing 53rd street. If you’re already inside MoMA, there’s a separate door by security. They have to let you in.
I didn’t have a reservation, but was seated immediately. Win!

I really should’ve asked questions instead of going rogue. My intention was to do the lunch prix fixe menu. The menu on the table was a la carte. This did however work out better for me as I had limited time since I was catching a broadway show.

Started with the olives then followed with the hot dogs and closed with the gem lettuce. They did come at different times. This gave me the perfect time to nibble slowly. The olives paired perfectly with the salad. The hot dogs were my favorite. The whole meal was perfectly balanced for me.

Just have to mention how amazing the service was. No table had anything waiting to be taken away because there was always someone walking around. At one point, one of the guys clocked I had just finished drinking my water and within seconds he was at my table refilling my glass. I mean c’mon.
Will took great care of me. He even suggested the dessert I ended up getting which was the peach cruller.
I’m gonna try to come back to do the lunch tasting before I go back home to LA.

We visited Manhatta on a Saturday for my birthday and had a wonderful experience. The restaurant is located on the 60th floor of 28 Liberty Street and offers breathtaking views of Lower Manhattan, the Statue of Liberty, Staten Island, and New York Harbor.

Before our table was ready, we waited in the lounge area and enjoyed the incredible views. A thoughtful touch was the personalized birthday note waiting on our table when we arrived, which made the occasion feel extra special.

The atmosphere was elegant but welcoming, and it was interesting to see that many other guests were also celebrating birthdays and special occasions there.

We came for lunch and ordered the two-course lunch menu. To start, we had the “Beef Tartare” and “Fluke Crudo”, followed by the “Grilled Sea Bass”, “Dry-Aged Burger”, and “Lobster Ravioli” for our mains. For dessert, we enjoyed the “Coconut Mousse” and paired the meal with red wine and the “Land of the Sun” cocktail. The restaurant has an excellent selection of red, white, and sparkling wines.

The service was friendly and attentive without ever making us feel rushed.. We took our time, enjoyed the food, the drinks, and the stunning views, making it a memorable birthday celebration.

Manhatta has officially become one of my favorite restaurants of all time.

The experience starts with the stunning views from the 60th floor overlooking New York City, but the food and service are what truly make this place special. Every member of the staff was warm, knowledgeable, and attentive without ever being overbearing.

We ordered the four-course menu and every course was outstanding. For the first course, we had the Jonah Crab with asparagus, apple, and sorrel, along with the Bluefin Tuna with jicama, shiso, and white soy vinaigrette. The crab was honestly the best crab dish I’ve ever eaten—sweet, delicate, and perfectly balanced. The tuna was equally impressive, incredibly fresh and beautifully prepared.

For the second course, we chose the Seared Scallop with nduja, watermelon radish, and pea shoots, as well as the Glazed Sweetbreads with morel mushrooms, arugula pesto, and horseradish. Both dishes were expertly executed and packed with flavor.

For our mains, we had the Butter Poached Lobster and the Lamb Loin & Rib. The lobster was excellent, but the real surprise was the Koshihikari rice—it was absolutely amazing and one of the most memorable components of the entire meal. The lamb was perfectly cooked and paired wonderfully with the fava bean pesto, almond, and pecorino.

Dessert was the Pistachio Cake with strawberry and crème fraîche chamomile ice cream, which was a fantastic ending to the meal.

We also enjoyed several mezcal cocktails and wine pairings throughout dinner, all of which complemented the food beautifully.

Between the breathtaking views, exceptional service, creative menu, and unforgettable dishes, Manhatta delivered one of the best dining experiences I’ve had in NYC. Highly recommended, and I can’t wait to come back.

The reservation for Tatiana is almost impossible to get and was lucky enough to score one. Started off with the high and dry cocktail and ordered a bunch of items to try:

Curry goat patties 10/10 - these were so delicious, the pastry was flaky and buttery and the inside was savory and had a delicious curry flavor. I loved the yogurt aioli which was refreshing and helped cut out the heaviness of the patty

Fried okra 10/10 - super addictive and the hot honey really enhanced the flavor

Egusi tortellini 8.5/10 - the tortellini itself was well made and al dente with a really interesting egusi filling. The sauce on the plate was also really delicious and paired well with the tortellini. I found the bits of crab to be pretty fishy and it was clearly frozen crab.

Jerk chicken wings 10/10 - this wasn't on the menu and was a special for the night. Wings were tender and the jerk bbq flavor was really well balanced with the yogurt dipping sauce. The jerk flavoring was subtle which I preferred

Braised oxtail 8/10 - the meat was super tender and flavorful and loved eating it with the rice and peas. I did find the sauce to be too salty for my taste

Bbq collard greens 2/10 - this was the worst dish of the meal. The braised beef chunks were chewy and overcooked and tasty as tough as beef jerky. The bbq sauce was so incredibly sweet and overpowered the entire dish, I felt like I was eating collard greens with sugar. The best part was the corn bread which was made well.

Mom duke's shrimp 10/10 - I was so impressed with the size and quality of the shrimp. The sauce was delicious and the shrimp was cooked to perfection. This is a must try.

Bodega special 7/10 - I understood the concept behind this dessert and found it pretty cool. However, I didn't find the cosmic brownie to be that good, it was pretty standard for a brownie. I did really enjoy the powdered donut ice cream and was fascinated how they made it taste so similar to powdered donut including the texture and consistency of the ice cream.

Overall, the food had bold flavors and really opened up my palate to some interesting flavors I don't typically have. The food was good but not amazing enough for me to fight for a reservation each month when it opens up. Service was friendly but they could have changed our plates without us asking and chasing them down. They also took away the serving utensils a few times and we had to chase them down to replace them. The restaurant is very loud which I found a bit too much for me and made it very difficult to have a decent conversation with my friends.

Tatiana absolutely lived up to the hype. From the moment we arrived, the atmosphere felt vibrant and welcoming, and the entire experience managed to be both elevated and comfortable at the same time.

What stood out most was the food. Every dish felt thoughtful and creative without being overly complicated. The flavors were bold, balanced, and memorable, and you can really see Chef Kwame Onwuachi’s influence throughout the menu. There were multiple dishes that had everyone at the table talking long after dinner was over. The cocktails were equally impressive and complemented the meal perfectly.

What made the night especially memorable was that a quick flash flood level rainstorm hit while we were dining. Despite the unexpected chaos outside, the staff handled everything with remarkable grace, professionalism, and composure. Rather than letting the weather impact the experience, they remained attentive, calm, and accommodating, making guests feel taken care of throughout the evening. It was a great example of hospitality at its best.

Tatiana is certainly a special occasion restaurant (friend’s birthday) but it never felt pretentious. Between the exceptional food, outstanding service, and the way the team navigated a challenging situation with such poise, it was one of the most memorable dining experiences I’ve had in New York City. Well worth the visit.

I still have a great deal of respect for Le Bernardin and hope this was just an off day because I remember thinking much more highly of the food before. I would happily return and hope for an experience that better matches the restaurant’s reputation.

Beautiful, understated, slightly dated decor and comfortable seating. Mario was an attentive waiter - consummate professional.

I chose the City Harvest menu - supporting a local nonprofit- for 94$. The lobster starter was lobster in mayonnaise with avocado between two discs of perfectly cooked potato. It was over-salted and the lobster didn’t shine. The sea bass second course was also over-salted, slightly undercooked and chewy with a strong cumin sauce. Unbalanced. The pistachio dessert featured four preparations- the ice cream being the most balanced and of beautiful texture.

Sadly, I was underwhelmed. Ripert, had he eaten the menu, would’ve certainly been upset. I came for what he is known for - brilliantly balanced ingredients with minimal intervention that lets the seafood shine. This was not my experience at Le Bernardin.

Great food, exciting entertainment by your own servers! I would highly recommend this 50 style restaurant if you’re looking for something unique in a very unique city!

We stopped in for breakfast. Catching the restaurant just a few minutes after it’s opening. There were plenty of seats for our larger group of seven, but our host quickly pointed out that the place can fill up very quickly during the rush-hour, especially over lunch and dinner in between Broadway shows playing nearby. Enjoying the variety of songs, which can be requested is more than enough reason to check this place out.

I thought the food was excellent. My family got a little bit of everything. My daughter’s bagel sandwich, which included a rainbow swirl in the dough of the bagel tasted amazing, they made our eggs to perfection. I was on my first trip to New York City and my cousin wanted to go to this place. We walked from our hotel as it wasn't too far.

There was a line but it moved along pretty quickly. We didn't wait much longer than 20 to 25 minutes... but we also went on a weekday, earlier in the evening for dinner, which helped with our shorter wait time.

We were seated on the upper level, which was like a diner, counter type seating... which we actually liked better as it gave us a great view of the performances by the staff!

A lot of the staff if not all are Broadway performers working until they get offered gigs on Broadway... which was fun about this place! The entertainment was worth the trip alone... and I would say the food was actually pretty decent...

I got chicken and waffles and besides not being able to finish it all, it tasted great to me. The others in my party liked their meals as well... which was a club sandwich, and chicken tenders... they also got shakes which were very good!

The guy I sat next to was nice too... everyone at the restaurant was just there to have a good time, so I had fun conversations with the people next to me.

The staff and performers were awesome and fun and nice! They also told us they had recently lost 8 servers to Broadway musicals, which is their goal... and it also felt great to support the performers there too and to see them along in their theatrical journeys!

I highly recommend trying this place... my only caution is to pay attention to your bill as they automatically add gratuity to your bill... but unless you read it, most people would just add gratuity not realizing (I think it was 18% or 20%) was already added... so I didn't leave an additional tip on top of that as we also gave the staff their own tip when they brought Phillip the Bucket around, which any money donated to that goes to helping them fulfill their Broadway dreams by getting headshots or other things they need... that money is dispersed to them, strictly for that purpose... so that's my only caution is that you are already tipping on your bill, so pay attention to that!

Otherwise, I don't have any complaints and the staff was great and I wish them the best!

text.text:
I recently visited 53 in Manhattan to celebrate Mother’s Day, and while we were excited to try it, the overall experience was disappointing.

For a restaurant charging over $150 per person, chipped bowls should never be brought to the table. When we asked the busboy to replace them, his reaction felt noticeably annoyed, which made the service feel unpolished for this level of dining.

I also think management should better train the team on menu guidance and recommendations. We mentioned that we were sharing plates and wanted to try a variety of dishes, but no one pointed out that we had ordered three rice-based items. A simple suggestion would have helped us balance the meal better with steak, seafood, or other options. Instead, we ended up eating multiple bowls of rice each.

The food itself was average. The highlights were the appetizers, especially the oysters with uni and the eel club, but neither felt especially memorable from a culinary standpoint. The lobster rice was the biggest disappointment. At $88 per order, the lobster tasted bland, mushy, and not very fresh. The ikura added most of the flavor, but without it, the dish would have been very flat. I also could not taste much aroma from the lotus leaf, so it felt more decorative than functional.

The clay pot rice dishes were better and at least met the basic expectations of what proper clay pot rice should look and taste like, but they were not enough to make the meal feel special.

Overall, this was probably a one-time visit for us. We dine around the city often and were genuinely looking forward to this meal, but between the chipped bowls, uneven service, limited menu guidance, and underwhelming food, the experience did not match the price point. For a restaurant at this level, these basics should be handled much better.

This is a very nice Asian fusion Chinese restaurant with a great atmosphere, but you need to make reservations in advance. Overall, the flavors are very solid.

I highly recommend their Foie Gras Custard (Foie Gras Steamed Egg) — it was incredibly rich, and the addition of mushrooms enhanced the overall umami.

However, the Foie Gras on Toast set had a slight flaw: the toast was a bit over-charred, which slightly overpowered the dish, and the Eel component was hard to taste.

The Lamb Ribs were decent but nothing extraordinary. The strong barbecue glaze slightly masked the natural flavor of the meat, though the preparation was quite creative.

The Kung Pao Quail was tasty and innovative — so tender that you wouldn’t even guess it was quail.

The Black Cod Clay Pot with Rice was rather average, nothing remarkable.

Overall, this restaurant is quite innovative. The flavors and techniques are authentic while keeping the creative fusion style. I would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a unique dining experience.

Came here for a slightly early dinner after a Broadway show with a party of 4 on a Sunday evening. We had a reservation, but it didn't seem like we would have needed one, but I suppose better safe than sorry. The ambiance feels straight of the golden age, which is an aesthetic I'm certainly a sucker for. Even their robust cocktail menu fits the bill and is one of the prettiest menus I've ever had the joy of perusing. Staff was able to sit us a little bit ahead of our reservation which was also much appreciated. Wait staff was also very helpful and attentive, I don't think I've ever had my water glass so topped off!

Starting off with cocktails, this place is a gin bar through and through and you'd be making a mistake if you didn't try one of their many options. I went with the 10,000 words, which you simply just give a spirit of your choice (I picked gin of course) and whether you antes) wanted your drink shaken or stirred and the bartender does the rest, so a bit of a surprise! I wound up with their version of The Last Word which was delightfully citrusy but I was hoping I'd wind up with something a little more adventurous app things considered. My girlfriend got the blackberry G&T, which was not only very pleasing to look at but delicious to boot.

For food, we started with splitting some zucchini blossoms and beef cheek bao buns (both come in portions of 3). Both were tasty, but I love a good bao bun and these were so light and pillowy, I could have just went for an order of those for my main course. For the entree I went for the roasted half chicken, perhaps the most unassuming choice on the menu but this was maybe the best roast chicken I've ever had. Prepared perfectly, cooked to perfection, excellent portion size, and the kicker of it all was the stunning gravy that I was tempted to lick my plate for. Chicken is very easy to screw up, and they nailed it on all fronts here. My girlfriend went for the Valerie Signature burger with white cheddar and this thing did not mess around! A very rich patty, cooked to her temperature of choice served alongside some garlic truffle fries that made an American classic feel just a little more elevated.

Our experience was delightful and I'd love to comeback here again, especially to check out more of the cocktail menu and soak in more of that golden age aura the place gives.

text.text:
Vita Verde has a beautiful atmosphere, modern décor, great vibes, and a very clean space. The service was friendly, attentive, and there was no wait. The cocktails were excellent and easily the highlight of the experience.

As someone who travels often and enjoys trying different cuisines, I was a bit disappointed with the food. I ordered the steak fajitas based on the bartender’s recommendation (“you can’t go wrong with them”), but they didn’t live up to the hype. The presentation was nice, but the portion was small, the steak was quite chewy, and the tortillas were served cold and dry.

What surprised me most was the flavor profile. The seasoning reminded me more of a mild curry or Indian-inspired spice blend than the bold, fresh flavors I typically expect from Mexican cuisine. It wasn’t bad, just unexpected and not particularly memorable.

That said, I’d definitely come back for the atmosphere, drinks, and service. I may give the food another shot and try a different dish next time—just not the fajitas.

This place went viral based off the drinks and the brunch atmosphere. I must say, everything you see that's viral take it with a grain of salt.

I will take ownership of the fact that, the birthday party seating amount was changed from 8 to 11 people. However, this was confirmed with the staff prior to arriving and they said they were okay with accommodating the large party. If they could not, they should have said so.

Food: Extremely small portions, overpriced and lacking flavor. We ordered tacos, and it was size of the bottom of a red solo cup, not even double tortilla, for a price point of $20 plus. I had steak over fries, I did not know they literally meant cut up steak over shoestring fries. What an absolute rip off for $27.00. Wings were ordered and they tasted like they were turning bad, we sent them back. Food is mediocre and lacking flavor, expensive for such small portions and just overall a disappointing experience. We had to get food after.

Tables/Seating: They squeezed in a table of 12 people on a tabletop of 3 tables. Absolutely ridiculous. I asked that they add a table or split the party to which the manager who appeared to be Irish kept saying he didn't have tables. I informed him they were getting paid regardless, so fix the problem, as we were sitting on top of each other. Sitting on stools with no backing, super uncomfortable, not to mention, we were by the door and the draft was cold, windy, coming through this heavy curtain that was useless.

Customer Service: Our server we had was rude, the manager was not polite, lacking customer service front of the house expertise, no sense of apologies for their shortcoming and the hostess is even more useless. I asked for a manager, she mentioned, she already addressed the issue with a guest from the party, I informed her this was not my question and my issue went above her pay grade. We had an issue with the bill and the server said she wasn't in "the mood" to deal with it. In addition to rushing us, walking away from the table when questions are asked, just overall disgusting with her attitude. We asked to remove her 20% automatic gratuity, as this is an option, so we could leave what we wanted.

Drinks: After 2 drinks, it becomes nauseating tasting the artificial flavor from the mimosas. I didn't understand why we paid for bottomless and instead of leaving the pitchers on the table with such a large party, server kept coming back, delayed. They tried forcing everyone to drink at the table, which how could you, if not everyone drinks and you have drivers? Nice little lawsuit on deck with this one.

Stay away from this location, they cram you into a small establishment, with tacky customer service and disgusting food for a price point which isn't reasonable at all. The manager, Irish male, dismissive, goes back and forth and I'm not really sure who's in charge of this puppet show. There are so many other locations in midtown and LES where you can get a better experience and bang for your buck.

For the taste, sounds, and excitement of Mexico, this establishment spans three vibrant levels where the fun never runs out.

Translated from the Spanish meaning “green life," we stopped at Vida Verde located off of 55th St in Midtown West for a drink, but it definitely would satisfy margarita lovers and other guacamole aficionados.

Upon entering, for some of us as first-timers, the patrons feel relaxed and have a nice time characterized by playful colors and modern accents that evoke energy in every corner of the space, the street-level dining room, and the bar. They also have a spacious mezzanine and an outdoor rooftop patio, weather permitting.

There was a live DJ in an upbeat party atmosphere, with various birthday celebrations taking place. This did not detract from the bartender providing us with excellent service.

Luckily, there were three seats available at the foot in the bar. We decided on Margaritas and a Sangria. The drinks were excellent, well crafted, and perfect for the afternoon.

Well worth the visit!

Everything I’ve tried has been top-notch—the oysters, sushi, Crab Louie salad, burger, lobster roll, butter cake, and carrot cake have all been excellent. The Ocean Roll is a particular standout, and the Hot & Dirty Martini, with olive-oil-infused Belvedere and Calabrian chili blue-cheese-stuffed Castelvetrano olives, is fantastic.

But what really makes me want to come back is the service. I’ve been fortunate enough to have Natasha take care of me four times now, and she is absolutely lovely. She’s warm, attentive, gracious, and has a wonderful way of making even a quick meal or drink at the bar feel special. Ocean Prime is already a great restaurant, but Natasha genuinely elevates the experience. I always look forward to seeing her when I come in.

The scallops were probably my favorite because they had a nice sear while staying tender inside, and the risotto underneath made the whole thing feel more substantial. The lobster linguine was messy in a very enjoyable way, with enough lobster that I wasn't just hunting around the pasta for pieces. The carrot cake was huge and rich, so sharing it would have been the smarter move.

The restaurant has a polished feel, but the food doesn't get lost behind it. I could see this working equally well for a special dinner or just an evening when you want seafood without going somewhere super casual.

text.text:
We visited Jams inside 1 Hotel Central Park for brunch and really enjoyed the atmosphere of the restaurant. The interior is beautiful, filled with lots of plants and greenery that make the space feel cozy, warm, and relaxing. The restaurant has a stylish but comfortable vibe, and it’s a nice place to slow down and enjoy brunch in the middle of Manhattan. The staff were friendly and welcoming throughout the visit.

The brunch menu offers a good mix of sweet and savory options, including dishes like French toast, pancakes, omelets, poached eggs, and bagels. Overall, the food and atmosphere made for a very enjoyable brunch experience.

We ordered the “Avocado Toast”, “Spring Frittata”, “Baja Breakfast”, and “Berry & Ricotta Buttermilk Pancakes”. Our favourite was definitely the Baja Breakfast, which had a really nice tangy flavour.

The only small challenge we had was when splitting the bill, as it seemed the supervisor was not very familiar with handling it, so we had to figure it out ourselves in the end. Other than that, it was a very pleasant brunch experience.

Wonderful breakfast place!! Our Saturday morning started off on the right foot because of our delicious food here.

We made a reservation (highly recommend) and were seated immediately. Service was incredibly kind and friendly. We ordered our drinks (a cappuccino and an orange juice), which did take a while.
